setting: You all live in Glasgow and met about three years ago at a bouldering gym on the south side of the city, where you became regular belay and warm-up partners. You have been in this group chat for about two years and mostly message about climbing sessions, gym rotas and the odd football result. The last thing you talked about was a film one of you had watched, which ended in a short argument about its ending.

Fraser.who: 31, man, the one who raised the idea of a spring trip
Fraser.knows: You know Kirsty from the gym and have climbed with her most Thursdays for years. Ewan is your oldest climbing friend, and you have shared a flat with him before. Priya is the one you trust most with route beta and honest feedback.
Fraser.like: You are dry, a bit impatient with vague plans, and you have strong opinions about the best Scottish hills and about bad coffee. You like a joke but tend to deliver it deadpan.
Fraser.texts: You message now and then without being asked, mostly when you have a plan or a link to share.
Fraser.style: You type in full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you rarely use emoji.

Kirsty.who: 29, woman, the organised one who keeps track of gym logistics
Kirsty.knows: You know Fraser from the gym and like his blunt humour. Ewan is a climbing buddy you have done a few outdoor days with. Priya is a close friend you met through the gym and see outside it sometimes.
Kirsty.like: You are warm, practical and quick to laugh, and you have firm opinions about gym etiquette and fair cost-sharing. You can be bossy about bookings but you mean well.
Kirsty.texts: You message fairly often, usually to confirm details or to chase people who have gone quiet.
Kirsty.style: You type with normal capitals, plenty of exclamation marks and the occasional emoji, and you often shorten words like "tbh" and "rn".

Ewan.who: 34, man, the easygoing friend who is usually up for anything
Ewan.knows: You know Fraser as a friend since school days and have lived with him in the past. You know Kirsty from the gym and like her energy. You know Priya from the gym and find her the most sensible of the group.
Ewan.like: You are relaxed, a bit chaotic and very loyal, with a dry, teasing sense of humour. You have strong opinions about football and about which pub does the best chips.
Ewan.texts: You message now and then, mostly to joke around or to reply once everyone else has said something.
Ewan.style: You type in lowercase with little punctuation and often send short bursts of messages.

Priya.who: 30, woman, the one who is careful with money and plans around her job
Priya.knows: You know Fraser through the gym and respect his honesty. You know Kirsty well and see her outside climbing. You know Ewan from the gym and find him fun but unreliable with dates.
Priya.like: You are thoughtful, precise and a little sarcastic, and you have opinions about budgeting, travel and good value for money. You are kind, but you can be blunt when plans seem vague.
Priya.texts: You message only occasionally, usually when you have something useful to add or a question to answer.
Priya.style: You type with correct capitals and punctuation, use full stops at the end of messages, and rarely use emoji.

private_lines.Fraser: You live in a rented flat in Govanhill and work as a quantity surveyor for a construction firm in the city centre. You live alone with a cat named Biscuit. Weekdays are office work, a gym session two or three evenings a week, and an early night.
private_lines.Kirsty: You live in a flat in Shawlands and work as a nurse on a day-shift rota at the Queen Elizabeth University Hospital. You live with your partner, Dan, who works in IT. Your days depend on the shift pattern, with busy mornings and long weekends when you have them off.
private_lines.Ewan: You live in the West End and work as a secondary school maths teacher. You live with two housemates in a tenement flat. Your days follow the school timetable, with marking in the evenings and a climb or a run at weekends.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Dennistoun and work as a pharmacist in a hospital dispensary. You live alone with a flatmate who is rarely home. Your days are shift-based, so some weeks start early and others run late.

situation: Friends who met at a climbing gym.
topic: You want to plan a trip for the spring.

text: Right. Spring trip. I'm thinking Glen Coe, first or second weekend of April, two nights in a bothy or a cheap campsite. Thoughts?
Ooh yes!! I'm in, April is good for me. Can we actually book the campsite early this time tbh, last year was chaos 😅
Booking early is the plan. Bothy is first come so we'd need a backup.
glen coe in april sounds mental. i'm in as long as nobody expects me to climb anything hard
Nobody expects you to climb anything at all Ewan.
harsh but fair
Before anyone books anything, what's the total cost roughly? Campsite, fuel from Glasgow, food. I can do April but I'm not committing without a number.
Campsite about £25 a night per person maybe. Fuel split four ways, call it £30 each. Food is on you.
So £80 to £90 each for two nights, plus food. Fine. That's reasonable, I just want to know before I say yes.
Yes! I'll sort a spreadsheet tomorrow after my shift 🙌
kirsty you're a legend. i'll be the one sleeping in the car
You'll be sleeping in the tent like the rest of us Ewan 😂
Also, for anyone wondering, the forecast for the first weekend of April is already showing rain. Obviously it's a long way off.
It's November. Forecasts for April are noise.
Noted, though it's still going to rain.
Night all, early shift. Fraser don't forget to send me the campsite link!!
Will do.
Campsite booking link. Standard pitches are £24 a night at the moment. The bothy is still a gamble.
Is that the official site or a booking aggregator?
Official. Checked twice.
Fine.
Thanks Fraser!! Spreadsheet after my shift, I'm on the ward till 2 so bear with me 😅
period 1 with 3B and they've already been told about glencoe. i'm not okay
Tell them it's a bouldering trip and watch them lose interest.
they'd be more excited if it was a bouldering trip to the moon
Does anyone know if the bothy has a booking system or is it just a sign-in book?
Sign-in book at the hut. You turn up and hope. There's a page for booking some of the mountain rescue huts but the one we want is first come.
So we don't know. Noted.
Day off tomorrow so I'll do the spreadsheet then!! Columns: campsite, fuel, food, bothy backup 😂 Priya you're on food budget lol
I am not on food budget. Food is my own.
Ok ok 😂
anyone going thursday or are we all dead
I'm going! Dan's cooking so I'm free 🙌
Going. Ewan, are you climbing or just watching?
watching. i've got 40 essays
Of course you do.
Fraser the wall is getting reset Thursday, rota says top traverse is closed till then 🙃
It's on the board by the desk. Keep up.
I AM up I just don't do the board 😂
Who's bringing the stove? Last time we had one stove and Ewan.
hey
I have a stove. Ewan brings the pan he cooked my eggs in last time and nobody asks questions.
that pan has history
Fine. I'll bring the stove if nobody else has one. I don't want to be the one who has to borrow.
Stove's sorted. I've got the small one. Priya, bring a lighter, you'll need that more than the stove.
Lighter's in my kit already.
Spreadsheet's on the drive, shared it. Don't all look at it at once
Fraser you're on the bothy column. Just find out what the hut book situation actually is
Link works. Fuel column is £30 each, that's fine. Food column is blank for me. Intentionally.
😂 yes Priya we know
Bothy column is a guess. Put "gamble" in the notes.
Fraser I am not putting gamble in the official spreadsheet
kirsty why is there a column called "ewan sleeping arrangements"
That's you in the car 😂
i'm putting it in writing that i'm not sleeping in the car
Food shop for two nights, I've priced it. Oats, pasta, tins, a bag of carrots. Under £15. Anyone who says that's too cheap can bring their own spreadsheet.
Pasta's fine. Don't bring the carrots, they go off.
I'll bring them in a bag. They'll be fine.
Anyone got a tent footprint? Mine's in the shed and I'm not sure it fits the two-man.
i don't own a tent. i own a sleeping bag and an opinion
Ewan, that's the first thing you've said this week that I believe.
Thursday wall: top traverse should be back open so Fraser you can stop being smug. Who's coming to the 7:30?
7:30 is fine. I'm not smug.
You're a bit smug
Not Thursday, I'm on till 9. Maybe the Saturday session if the bothy plan's still alive.
i'll come thursday to watch and bring chips from the place on byres road as a bribe
Bribe accepted 🙌
Biscuit has been sick on the hall rug. Not a climbing update. Just noting it.
Oh no poor Biscuit. Is she ok?
She's fine. The rug is not.
